title: Backend: help-center write routes only require a user token, so any registered account can publish public help-center articles and categories
description:
## Summary

The help-center write routes are grouped in a variable named `helpcenterAdminUrl`, but that group applies only `middleware.Authorize`. There is no admin, staff or role check, so **any registered account** - a brand-new user in any organisation - can create help-center categories and publish articles. The matching read routes are public (no auth), so the content the attacker creates is immediately served to anonymous visitors from the product's own help center.

## Where

- `pkg/router/helpcenter.go:19` - `helpcenterAdminUrl := r.Group(fmt.Sprintf("%v", ApiVersion), middleware.Authorize(db.Postgresql))`.
- `pkg/router/helpcenter.go:23-24` - `POST /help-center/categories` and `POST /help-center/articles/:category-id` are mounted on that group.
- `pkg/router/helpcenter.go:27-32` - the read routes (`/help-center/categories`, `/help-center/articles/:id`, `/help-center/articles/search`) are on `helpcenterUrl`, which has no middleware at all, so freshly created content is public immediately with no review or publish flag.
- `pkg/controller/helpcenter/helpcenter_category.go:14-44` (`CreateHelpCenterCategory`) and `pkg/controller/helpcenter/helpcenter.go:25-54` (`CreateHelpCenterArticle`) never read `userClaims`, never check an admin/staff role, and store no author id.
- Contrast: every other back-office write route is protected by `middleware.AdminAuthorize` (`pkg/router/admin.go:20`) or `middleware.RequireSuperAdmin()` (`pkg/router/admin.go:57`). The help-center routes are the only CMS writes that rely on a plain user token.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Register or sign in as an ordinary user in any organisation and copy the access token.
2. Create a category:

   `curl -X POST "https://<host>/api/v1/help-center/categories" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"name":"Billing","description":"Payments and invoices"}'`

   -> `201 Created` with the new category id.
3. Publish an article in it:

   `curl -X POST "https://<host>/api/v1/help-center/articles/<category_id>" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"title":"Refund policy","content":"Send payments to ..."}'`

   -> `201 Created` `"Article added successfully"`.
4. Read it back **without any token**:

   `curl "https://<host>/api/v1/help-center/articles/<article_id>"`

   -> `200 OK` with the attacker-authored article, served as official help-center content.

## Expected

- `403` for any caller who is not a platform/support admin, and an author/moderation record on the created rows.

## Actual

- `201 Created` for any authenticated user, and the content is immediately public.

## Potential impact

Because help-center articles are public and rendered on the product's own domain, this is a content-injection / trust-abuse primitive: an ordinary user can publish arbitrary instructions (for example payment-redirection or credential-phishing copy) under the Zedu help center, and can pollute the category list that every visitor sees.

## Suggested fix

- Protect `helpcenterAdminUrl` with `middleware.AdminAuthorize(db.Postgresql)` (or a dedicated support-role guard) and keep the public read group separate.
- Add `author_id` / `status` (draft, published) columns and serve only published rows on the public routes.

Source links: [https://github.com/Zedu-Endor/zedu-be/blob/67db4db20f1876a644f6b305575303aa312c5ce0/pkg/router/helpcenter.go#L19](https://github.com/Zedu-Endor/zedu-be/blob/67db4db20f1876a644f6b305575303aa312c5ce0/pkg/router/helpcenter.go#L19), [https://github.com/Zedu-Endor/zedu-be/blob/67db4db20f1876a644f6b305575303aa312c5ce0/pkg/controller/helpcenter/helpcenter.go#L25](https://github.com/Zedu-Endor/zedu-be/blob/67db4db20f1876a644f6b305575303aa312c5ce0/pkg/controller/helpcenter/helpcenter.go#L25), [https://github.com/Zedu-Endor/zedu-be/blob/67db4db20f1876a644f6b305575303aa312c5ce0/pkg/router/admin.go#L20](https://github.com/Zedu-Endor/zedu-be/blob/67db4db20f1876a644f6b305575303aa312c5ce0/pkg/router/admin.go#L20)
